title: Tidy up includes in `scene/main` and `scene/debugger`
body:
Helps address #111218, though I haven't benchmarked any potential gains in compile time.

This was just me almost meditatively going through the includes in `scene/main` (main goal) and `scene/debugger` (why not, it's just a few extra files) to try to minimize what is included in the headers, and tidy up the .cpp.

Some of the changes are debatable, sometimes forward declares go a bit overboard and replacing a `node.h` include by most of what it includes anyway is not necessary a big gain.

Some takeaways:

- `viewport.h`, `window.h` and `status_indicator.h` include `display_server.h` just for some enums or typedefs. Those might be candidate for moving to a dedicated file so we don't pull all of `display_server.h` in the ubiquitous `viewport.h` and `window.h` (includes Image, Resource, OS, notably). Not touch in this PR, but `display_server.h` is also included in `rendering_server.h` and `rendering_device.h` just for `DisplayServer::WindowID` (i.e. `int`).
- `node.h` includes are already as minimal as can be, though I notice we can't forward-declare InputEvent anymore due to the required argument changes which needs fully specified types. I guess that's a tradeoff we have to live with.
- `scene_tree.cpp` really does too much stuff... thankfully it's a `.cpp`.
- We still have too many files which define multiple classes, and oftentimes some of those other classes aren't needed as often as the base class. E.g. `viewport.h` defines ViewportTexture which is only used in a few files. Moving it to its own file could almost allow removing `texture.h` as a dependency in `viewport.h`... almost, because there's `get_vrs_texture()` which returns Texture2D too in Viewport (which is another thing I've noted, some classes accumulated system-specific APIs like VRS here for rendering/XR which also increase their dependencies).
- As noted in #111218, one of the hottest includes is `ref_counted.h`, mostly for the `Ref<T>` class. `ref_counted.h` is already relatively lean but depends on `class_db.h` which is pretty big. I wonder how feasible it would be to move `Ref<T>` to a dedicated header that wouldn't depend on `class_db.h`.
  * _Edit:_ Tried briefly, `Ref<T>::unref()` does a `reinterpret_cast<RefCounted *>` so we can't get away with a forward-declare or not including `ref_counted.h` in `ref.h`, which defeats its purpose.
